# Judicium Arbitration

> Premier arbitration and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) law firm in North India. 20+ years of experience, 500+ commercial disputes resolved across 20+ practice areas. Offices in New Delhi (HQ), Gurgaon, Noida, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Panipat, Prayagraj, and Lucknow.

Judicium Arbitration represents clients in domestic and international commercial arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended in 2015, 2019, and 2021). The firm handles institutional arbitration before DIAC, MCIA, ICC, SIAC, and LCIA; ad-hoc arbitration; mediation and conciliation; Section 9 and Section 17 interim relief applications; emergency arbitrator proceedings; setting aside and enforcement proceedings; and foreign award enforcement under the New York Convention.

Practice areas span dispute resolution, banking and finance, corporate and commercial, capital markets, private equity, intellectual property, real estate and urban development, projects and infrastructure, insolvency and bankruptcy, competition and antitrust, labour and employment, data privacy and cybersecurity, insurance, technology / media / telecommunications, healthcare and life sciences, international trade and WTO, white collar crime, and defence / aviation / space.

Contact: Judiciumarbitration@gmail.com | +91-9899686394

## Services (notice, recovery and compliance work)

- [Legal Services](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services): Hub for the firm's service lines - what to do when a notice, a dishonoured cheque or an unpaid invoice has already landed.

- [GST Notice Reply and Litigation](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/gst-notice-reply): A GST notice that goes unanswered becomes an ex parte order, and the demand then has to be challenged on appeal with a pre-deposit instead of answered on the merits.
- [Income Tax Notice Reply and Representation](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply): Under faceless assessment the reply you upload is largely the case on record — there is no later hearing at which to repair a thin response.
- [Cheque Bounce and Section 138 Proceedings](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/cheque-bounce-section-138): The thirty-day notice window runs from the bank return memo, not from when you noticed. It cannot be extended, and once it closes the Section 138 remedy is lost for that cheque.
- [Money Recovery and MSME Samadhaan](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/money-recovery-msme-samadhaan): Recovery claims are subject to a three-year limitation period. Part payments and written acknowledgements reset it, but silence does not — and a time-barred claim cannot be revived.
- [Legal Notice — Drafting and Reply](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/legal-notice-drafting-reply): A reply is not optional in substance. Silence is routinely pleaded as acquiescence, and an unanswered allegation is harder to dispute later than one denied at the time.
- [Labour Court and Employment Disputes](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/labour-court-employment-disputes): A reference of an individual termination under Section 2A must ordinarily be made within three years of the date of discharge. Conciliation should be initiated well before that.
- [Company Registration and ROC Compliance](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/company-registration-roc-compliance): Late filing fees under Section 403 accrue at a fixed amount per day with no cap, and continued default can disqualify directors under Section 164(2) for five years across every company they hold office in.
- [Trade Licence and Business Registrations](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/trade-licence-business-registration): Operating without a required licence, or on a lapsed one, exposes the business to sealing, penalty and prosecution under the relevant municipal or sectoral statute.

Each service page carries Service + FAQPage + HowTo schema with the governing statutes, the forums the matter is heard in, the step-by-step process and the statutory deadline that applies.
## Notice types (what to do about a specific notice)

Pages for the exact notice a client has received, each stating the statutory deadline, the consequence of missing it, and what the reply must address.

- [GST DRC-01 Show Cause Notice](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/gst-notice-reply/drc-01-show-cause-notice) - Form DRC-01 · Section 73 / 74, CGST Act. The reply is due within the period stated in the notice, ordinarily 30 days. The adjudication order must then be passed within three years of the annual return due date under Section 73, or five years under Section 74.
- [GST DRC-01A Intimation of Liability](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/gst-notice-reply/drc-01a-intimation) - Form DRC-01A · Rule 142(1A), CGST Rules. Part B of Form DRC-01A — the reply — is ordinarily due within 15 days, or such period as the intimation states.
- [GST ASMT-10 Scrutiny Notice](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/gst-notice-reply/asmt-10-scrutiny-notice) - Form ASMT-10 · Section 61, CGST Act. The explanation is due in Form ASMT-11 within 30 days of service, or such further period as the officer permits.
- [GST REG-17 Registration Cancellation Notice](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/gst-notice-reply/reg-17-cancellation-notice) - Form REG-17 · Section 29, CGST Act. The reply in Form REG-18 is due within seven working days of service. If cancellation has already been ordered, revocation is applied for in Form REG-21, ordinarily within 30 days of the order.
- [GST Appeal in Form APL-01](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/gst-notice-reply/apl-01-gst-appeal) - Form APL-01 · Section 107, CGST Act. Three months from communication of the order, extendable by one further month on sufficient cause shown. The limitation is strict and the Supreme Court has held that the Limitation Act does not extend it beyond that further month.
- [Income Tax Notice under Section 143(2)](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-143-2-scrutiny-notice) - Section 143(2), Income-tax Act. The notice must be served within three months from the end of the financial year in which the return was filed. Your responses are due by the dates specified on the portal, usually 15 days per notice.
- [Income Tax Notice under Section 148](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-148-reassessment-notice) - Section 148, Income-tax Act. The return in response is due within the period stated in the notice. More importantly, the notice itself must be within the Section 149 limitation: ordinarily three years from the end of the relevant assessment year, extending to ten where escaped income represented as an asset or expenditure exceeds fifty lakh rupees.
- [Income Tax Notice under Section 148A(b)](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-148a-b-show-cause) - Section 148A(b), Income-tax Act. Not less than seven days and not more than thirty days from service, or such further period as allowed on application. The officer must then pass an order under Section 148A(d) deciding whether it is a fit case to issue a notice.
- [Income Tax Notice under Section 139(9)](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-139-9-defective-return) - Section 139(9), Income-tax Act. Fifteen days from intimation, extendable on application to the assessing officer.
- [Income Tax Intimation under Section 245](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-245-refund-adjustment) - Section 245, Income-tax Act. Ordinarily thirty days from the intimation to respond on the portal, agreeing or disagreeing with the demand and stating reasons.
- [Income Tax Demand Notice under Section 156](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-156-demand-notice) - Section 156, Income-tax Act. Thirty days from service, unless a shorter period is permitted. An appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) must be filed within thirty days of the order.
- [Income Tax Penalty Notice under Section 271](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/income-tax-notice-reply/section-271-penalty-notice) - Sections 270A / 271, Income-tax Act. The reply is due within the period stated, commonly 15 to 30 days. The penalty order itself is subject to limitation under Section 275.
- [Employer Show Cause and Termination Letter — Reply](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/labour-court-employment-disputes/termination-show-cause-reply) - Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The period stated in the notice, commonly 48 hours to 7 days. A reference of an individual termination under Section 2A must ordinarily be raised within three years of discharge.
- [Labour Commissioner Conciliation Notice](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/labour-court-employment-disputes/labour-commissioner-conciliation-notice) - Section 12, Industrial Disputes Act. The date fixed in the notice. Conciliation proceedings are expected to conclude within fourteen days of commencement, though extensions are common in practice.
- [Section 138 Demand Notice](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/cheque-bounce-section-138/section-138-demand-notice) - Section 138(b), Negotiable Instruments Act. Within thirty days of receiving the bank's return memo. The drawer then has fifteen days from receipt to pay. The complaint must be filed within one month of that fifteen-day period expiring.
- [Reply to a Legal Notice Received](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/legal-notice-drafting-reply/reply-to-legal-notice) - Pre-litigation correspondence. The period stated in the notice, commonly fifteen to thirty days. Statutory notices have fixed periods — a Section 138 demand gives fifteen days to pay, a Section 8 IBC notice ten days to respond.
- [MSME Samadhaan Reference — Delayed Payment](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/money-recovery-msme-samadhaan/msme-samadhaan-reference) - Section 18, MSMED Act, 2006. The reference may be filed once payment is overdue beyond the appointed day. The Council is required to conclude within ninety days of the reference, though in practice it often runs longer. The underlying claim remains subject to the three-year limitation period.
- [Summary Suit Demand under Order XXXVII](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/services/money-recovery-msme-samadhaan/order-37-summary-suit) - Order XXXVII, Code of Civil Procedure. The defendant has ten days from service of summons to enter appearance, and then ten days from service of the summons for judgment to apply for leave to defend. Missing either is decisive. The claim itself is subject to the three-year limitation.

## Cornerstone insights articles

- [Section 9 vs Section 17 of the Arbitration Act](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/section-9-vs-section-17-arbitration-act): When to approach a court vs the tribunal for interim relief.
- [What NN Global Means for Arbitration Agreements in India](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/nn-global-stamping-arbitration-agreements): Stamping and enforceability of arbitration clauses, 2024–2026.
- [Enforcing Foreign Arbitral Awards in India under the New York Convention](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/foreign-award-enforcement-india-new-york-convention): Part II Arbitration Act procedure, Section 48 grounds, and timelines.
- [DIAC vs MCIA vs IAMC](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/diac-vs-mcia-choosing-arbitral-institution-india): Choosing between India's leading arbitral institutions.
- [RERA and Arbitration: Builder-Buyer Disputes](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/rera-arbitration-builder-buyer-disputes-india): Why builder-buyer disputes are non-arbitrable, and where arbitration still applies in real estate.
- [Emergency Arbitrator Orders in India after Amazon v. Future Retail](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/emergency-arbitrator-india-amazon-future-retail): How emergency arbitrator awards became enforceable in India-seated arbitration via Section 17.
- [Section 11 Arbitrator Appointment after In Re Interplay (2023)](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/section-11-arbitrator-appointment-in-re-interplay): The narrowed scope of judicial scrutiny at the appointment stage and the stamping question.
- [The Cost of Arbitration in India (2026)](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/cost-of-arbitration-in-india): Arbitrator fees under the Fourth Schedule, institutional charges, and who pays under Section 31A.
- [How to Enforce an Arbitral Award in India](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/how-to-enforce-arbitral-award-india): Step-by-step enforcement under Section 36, the no-automatic-stay rule, and Order XXI execution.
- [Setting Aside an Arbitral Award under Section 34](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/section-34-challenge-arbitral-award): Grounds, the three-month timeline, patent illegality, and strategy.
- [Seat vs Venue of Arbitration in India](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/seat-vs-venue-arbitration-india): How the seat fixes the supervisory court — the BALCO and BGS SGS SOMA tests.
- [Drafting an Arbitration Clause for Indian Contracts](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/arbitration-clause-drafting-checklist-india): A practical checklist — seat, number of arbitrators, institution, scope, stamping.
- [SARFAESI vs DRT vs IBC](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/sarfaesi-vs-drt-vs-ibc-recovery-route): Choosing the right lender recovery route, with a side-by-side comparison.
- [MSME Delayed-Payment Claims under Section 18 of the MSMED Act](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/insights/msme-delayed-payment-section-18-msmed-act): The 45-day rule, 3x bank-rate interest, and the Facilitation Council route.

## Glossary

- [Arbitration & Commercial Law Glossary](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/glossary): Plain-English definitions of 30 key Indian arbitration, insolvency, banking, real-estate and corporate law terms — Section 9, Section 11, seat vs venue, CIRP, SARFAESI, RERA, Section 18 MSMED Act and more.

Each glossary term also has a dedicated, citation-ready page at `/glossary/{term-slug}` (e.g. https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/glossary/section-9-arbitration-act, /glossary/seat-of-arbitration, /glossary/cirp, /glossary/sarfaesi-act, /glossary/new-york-convention) answering "what is {term}?" with a one-sentence definition, a practical explanation, and the governing statutes.

## Practice areas (high-priority)

- [Arbitration & Alternative Dispute Resolution](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/arbitration-alternative-dispute-resolution): Flagship practice covering domestic, international commercial, and investment treaty arbitration; DIAC/MCIA/ICC/SIAC/LCIA proceedings; Section 9 and Section 17 emergency relief; award enforcement.
- [Banking & Finance](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/banking-finance): SARFAESI, DRT proceedings, NCLT applications, loan recovery, fraud investigations, regulatory compliance under RBI norms.
- [Corporate & Commercial](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/corporate-commercial): Companies Act 2013, contract drafting, shareholder disputes, joint ventures, corporate governance.
- [Real Estate & Urban Development](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/real-estate-urban-development): RERA proceedings, builder-buyer disputes, conveyancing, title due diligence, land acquisition.
- [Intellectual Property Rights](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/intellectual-property-rights): Patent, trademark, copyright, design; infringement litigation; IP licensing; IP-related arbitration.
- [Insolvency & Bankruptcy](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/insolvency-bankruptcy): IBC 2016 proceedings, CIRP, liquidation, NCLT and NCLAT representation.
- [Dispute Resolution & Litigation](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/dispute-resolution-litigation): Commercial court litigation, Supreme Court and High Court matters, civil and commercial disputes.
- [Capital Markets](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/capital-markets): SEBI compliance, IPO advisory, securities disputes, listing obligations.
- [Competition & Antitrust](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/competition-antitrust): CCI proceedings, merger control, abuse of dominance, cartel investigations.
- [Data Privacy & Cybersecurity](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/data-privacy-cybersecurity): DPDP Act 2023 compliance, IT Act, breach response.
- [Labour & Employment](https://www.judiciumarbitration.com/practice-areas/labour-employment): Industrial Disputes Act, POSH compliance, employment contracts, wrongful termination.
